The Great Corgiville Kidnapping.about: Tasha Tudor's sequel to Corgiville Fair. Part-time detective Caleb Corgi grows suspicious of a band of raccoons when the town's prize rooster goes missing. Watercolour corgis, goats and boggarts in Tudor's detailed 19th-century world. Ages 4–8.

The Sleeping Beauty — pop-up book.about: The fairy tale brought to life in three-dimensional pop-up scenes by illustrator Phillida Gili (who also made the pop-up Nutcracker). Oblong format with ribbon ties.

The Tale of Peter Rabbit — pop-up book.about: Beatrix Potter's naughty rabbit in Mr. McGregor's garden, retold with pop-up scenes built from the original illustrations.

The River Bank and Other Stories from Th.about: The first half of Kenneth Grahame's classic — Mole, Rat, Badger and Toad on the river — in a large-format edition with Inga Moore's luminous pen-and-watercolour illustrations of the English countryside. Ages 8 and up.

The New England Butt'ry Shelf Almanac.about: A month-by-month collection of New England people, birds, flowers, herbs, weather lore, customs and old recipes, illustrated in colour and black-and-white by Tasha Tudor. A cosy book for the kitchen shelf.

The Night Before Christmas.about: Clement C. Moore's 1822 poem in the edition many consider the cosiest of all: Tasha Tudor's candlelit watercolours of a New England farmhouse on Christmas Eve, complete with corgis. Ages 4–8.

Red Riding Hood.about: Beatrix Potter's own retelling of Perrault's tale, written over a century ago but never illustrated until Greenaway Medalist Helen Oxenbury took it on in 2019. Slightly darker than the usual version, with an English summer landscape and a very hungry wolf.

Here Comes Mother Goose.about: Over 60 nursery rhymes chosen by folklorist Iona Opie and illustrated by Rosemary Wells (of Max & Ruby fame). Big bold type and expressive animals — a read-aloud favourite for ages 2–5. Sequel to My Very First Mother Goose.

Celtic Calligraphy.about: A practical guide inspired by the Book of Kells and the Lindisfarne Gospels: how to form Celtic letters and add knotwork and glowing decoration, with simple projects and over 35 step-by-step photographs.

Lettering & Calligraphy.about: Joan Freeman's guide to the whole field of lettering, calligraphy and illumination — tools, construction, planning, colour — produced entirely from the author's own hand-lettered pages.

Celtic Design: A Sourcebook of Patterns.about: More than 1,500 black-and-white and colour Celtic patterns — knotwork, spirals, key patterns, animals — for designers, crafters and anyone who loves the style.

Winnie-the-Pooh: The Complete Collection.about: All four of A. A. Milne's Pooh books in one volume — Winnie-the-Pooh, The House at Pooh Corner, When We Were Very Young and Now We Are Six — with E. H. Shepard's original illustrations in colour.

Great Diaries.about: A big illustrated tour of the world's most remarkable diaries, journals and letters, from Samuel Pepys and Captain Scott to Virginia Woolf, Frida Kahlo and Anne Frank — with facsimile pages and the stories behind them. Foreword by historian Kate Williams.

The Flowers of William Morris.about: Which flowers did William Morris draw, and where did he find them? A richly illustrated look at the plants behind the famous wallpapers and textiles, with Morris's designs set beside the real flowers.

The Country Set.about: Fifty British birds and animals painted by Hannah Dale of Wrendale Designs in her quirky watercolour style, each with a short, funny character portrait. A small gift book for nature lovers.

The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck — pop-up.about: Six pop-up spreads closely following Beatrix Potter's original illustrations: Jemima looks for a safe place to lay her eggs and meets a very polite gentleman with sandy whiskers.

Piglet Is Entirely Surrounded by Water.about: A complete chapter from Winnie-the-Pooh as a stand-alone picture book: it rains and rains, Piglet is trapped by the flood, and his 'missage' in a bottle reaches Pooh. E. H. Shepard's illustrations in colour.

Mucha.about: A compact introduction to Alphonse Mucha, master of Art Nouveau: the Sarah Bernhardt posters, decorative panels, jewellery and paintings, with about 100 illustrations and a concise biography.

Beatrix Potter: At Home in the Lake Dist.about: Susan Denyer, who helped restore Hill Top for the National Trust, tells the story of Beatrix Potter's farmhouse, garden and Lake District landscapes — the real settings of the little books — with extracts from Potter's letters and diaries and photographs.

Fairy Stories and Rhymes.about: Four of Cicely Mary Barker's stories and rhyme collections in one large-format volume: The Lord of the Rushie River, Simon the Swan, Old Rhymes for All Times and The Fairy Necklaces, with her delicate illustrations.

Moomin: The Complete Lars Jansson Comic.about: The first volume drawn and written entirely by Lars Jansson, Tove's brother, who took over the London Evening News strip. Four stories: Moomin's Lamp, Moomin and the Railway, Moominpappa and the Spies, Moomin and the Circus. Black-and-white, large format.

The Nutcracker.about: Alexandre Dumas's retelling of E. T. A. Hoffmann's tale — gentler than the original and the version that inspired Tchaikovsky's ballet. Marie's ugly wooden nutcracker comes to life at midnight to battle the Mouse King.
